FOUNDATION PRACTICAL: SYNTHETIC SOURCE SNAPSHOT AND DICTIONARY
Original author-created teaching case, 2026-10-07, edition boundary2026-10-06.
NO actual firm, bank statement, observation, policy experiment or market rate.
Scenario dates in April2025 are fictional timestamps supplied to test timing.
The authoritative record-level snapshot is foundation-practical-data.json; no external
source, account, license or network access is needed. All case prose/code are
original. The manifest fingerprints local JSON and this notes file, not truth.

CURRENCY AND TIME
All input monetary amounts are integer USD cents; displayed/model quantities
are converted to USD exactly by dividing by100. Ledger covers7April2025 only.
Opening balances precede that day; reported closing cash follows all nine
transactions. Forecast origin is8April12:00UTC; saved source snapshot is
12April12:00UTC. A timestamp endingZ denotes UTC. Dates are observation days,
not release times. Source versions remain available even after a revision.

LEDGER DICTIONARY
Opening: cash2000, receivables300, equipment1000, supplier payables200,
loan600, equity2500 USD. Assets3300=liabilities800+equity2500.
L1 collect200 from opening receivables: cash+200, receivables-200.
L2 invoice900 current services on credit: receivables+900, revenue/equity+900.
L3 collect600 against L2: cash+600, receivables-600, no second revenue.
L4 pay400 current consumed operating expenses: cash-400, expense/equity-400.
L5 receive/consume150 supplies on credit: payables+150, expense/equity-150.
L6 pay100 against opening supplier balance: cash-100, payables-100.
L7 borrow500: cash+500, loan+500, no revenue.
L8 repay50 principal: cash-50, loan-50, no expense.
L9 owner withdrawal120: cash-120, equity-120, no operating expense.
Reported closing cash2630USD is an independent supplied statement component.
No tax, interest accrual, depreciation, inventory carryover, other valuation
change or other transaction occurs in this one-day model. Equipment proposal
is unexecuted and excluded from this historical ledger. No legal/accounting
standard is claimed; apply these explicitly supplied economic classifications.

OPERATING RECORDS
Each record is one active day with a known scheduled job count and daily total
variable consumables cost; it is NOT full company operating expense or revenue.
It is a different day/scope from the7April company ledger. Do not add these
selected sample costs to that ledger. Scheduled counts are known at
feature_available_at. They describe committed jobs for these teaching records.
All records are active, including D1's observed zero jobs and zero cost.
A null missing_reason accompanies released data. D6 has no cost releases;
its missing_reason is not_reported_by_snapshot, NOT zero or inactivity.
Each cost_releases entry has a positive consecutive version, an availability
instant and nonnegative integer cost_cents. Releases follow the observation
period. The latest release no later than a cutoff is the eligible version.
D1:1April, jobs0, first cost0 USD released2April09:00UTC.
D2:2April, jobs1, first cost4 USD released3April09:00UTC.
D3:3April, jobs2, first cost4 USD released4April09:00UTC; revised cost8 USD
    released11April09:00UTC, after the8April forecast origin.
D4:4April, jobs3, first cost10 USD released5April09:00UTC.
D5:9April, jobs4 known8April09:00UTC; first cost15 USD released10April09:00UTC.
D6:10April, jobs5 known8April09:00UTC; cost still unreported at snapshot.
The forecast protocol fits D1-D4 using latest origin-eligible costs and freezes
that model for D5/D6. Evaluation uses each target's first release available by
snapshot; no label produces null error/loss. Revision-aware re-fitting after
origin is a separate later descriptive analysis, never a past forecast input.

CAPITAL DECISION ASSUMPTIONS
At time0, after the observed ledger and before any new transactions, consider
an indivisible machine for500USD cash. Keep at least2000USD cash immediately
after purchase. No new borrowing for this proposal; operating cash later is
not part of that immediate constraint. No taxes, resale, extra capital charges
or other consequences beyond the explicit inputs. Time1/time2 are one/two
full years after purchase. Effective annual NOMINAL discount rate25% is an
assumed toy opportunity rate, not a quoted product, APR or measured market rate.
All savings and foregone rent are nominal USD paid at those year ends.
One high-demand state, probability4/5, gives gross savings450USD each year;
one low state, probability1/5, gives250USD each year. These probabilities and
savings are stipulated, not estimated from the operating sample or regression.
Using the space sacrifices50USD rent each year, an incremental opportunity
cost even though no rent-payment invoice appears in the observed ledger.
Defer gives zero incremental payoff in either state. Preferences are risk
neutral; compare expected time0 NPVs, subject to the immediate reserve.
State persists for both payments: do not draw independent yearly states.
Loss is foregone statewise best NPV (regret), in time0USD. It is not squared
forecast error, and this loss definition is distinct from utility risk aversion.

SIMULATION
400 iid model replications using random.Random(40517). Each replication draws
ONE state for the full two-year project with exact rational-probability integer
tickets. Enumerate the two states first for the exact expectation and variance.
Simulation illustrates numerical error only; it supplies no empirical sample,
parameter estimation, causal evidence or additional real-world information.
Record runtime because higher-level random routines can change across versions.
Use the full fixed run, never choose a seed/stopping time to change the decision.

VALIDATION AND ALLOWED CHANGES
Keep the original package immutable. Units, schema, keys, canonical dates and
protocol are fixed. All amounts use integer types, bounded nonnegative cents;
probabilities are exact fraction strings summing to1. An added duplicate record,
bool cost, zero/negative probability or cost release before its observation day
must fail. A changed ledger amount with the reported closing cash unchanged
must fail cash reconciliation. A separately labeled price520USD scenario is a
valid sensitivity case: feasibility remains but the expected-NPV choice changes.
The source snapshot's version history is not to be overwritten during any test.
